subtitle: Lesson 1 · Architect vs. Engineer

steps.label: Scope: one system
steps.sub: a firewall rule set, an IAM policy, one EDR deployment

steps.label: Horizon: days to weeks
steps.sub: fix the finding, close the ticket, pass the test

eyebrow: The architect's job, one layer up
code:
Engineer's question:
  "How do I implement this control correctly?"

Architect's question:
  "Which controls should exist at all, how do they fit
   together, and what are we trading away to get there?"
caption: The architect rarely writes the rule — they write the standard an engineer implements.

eyebrow: The industry already formalized this split

steps.label: NIST SP 800-181 (NICE Framework)
steps.sub: separates a Security Architecture specialty from implementation/operations roles

steps.label: CISSP CBK
steps.sub: "Security Architecture and Engineering" is its own domain, distinct from operational domains

code:
Pentest finds the same flaw on 12 systems.

Engineer:   fixes the 12 findings, closes 12 tickets.
Architect:  asks why the pattern keeps recurring,
            redesigns the SDLC gate or base image
            so a 13th instance structurally can't happen.
caption: Both responses are correct — for their respective jobs.
